transcript.text: fridge part freezin stuff, lettuce + yoghurts frozen solid at the back. hotpoint ff. any ideas pls

Yes — the usual reason is either the fridge being set too cold, or food sitting against the cold back wall/air outlet. Lettuce and yoghurts are especially prone to freezing there. 1. Check the fridge setting. Aim for about 3–5°C (or move a numbered dial towards the middle rather than its coldest setting). Turn off any fast-freeze/super-cool mode if fitted. This is the most common simple fix.
2. Move food 2–3 cm away from the rear wall and any vents; don’t pack the fridge tightly. If only items at the back freeze, this may be all that is needed.
3. Leave it for 24 hours with the door kept shut as much as possible. If food elsewhere is still freezing despite a sensible setting and clear space at the back, the temperature control may not be regulating properly — commonly the thermostat/sensor or an air flap. Is the fridge control set very cold or is fast-freeze/super-cool on, and were the frozen items touching the back wall?
dial's on max/coldest, kids might have moved it. and yes the frozen stuff is right against the back wall by the vent slots, fridge is rammed after big shop

That combination is very likely the cause rather than a failed part: the dial is on maximum cold, food is against the coldest area, and a packed fridge restricts airflow. 1. Turn the dial back to roughly the middle — not maximum cold. If it has temperature markings, aim for 3–5°C.
2. Move food away from the back wall and vent slots by a few centimetres, especially salad, dairy and anything with a high water content. Avoid tightly packing the fridge so air can circulate.
3. Keep the door shut as much as practical and allow about 24 hours for it to settle. The items already frozen may not recover in quality, but newly stored food should stop freezing. If food is still freezing in other areas of the fridge after that, with the dial at a sensible mid-setting and the vents clear, then the temperature control system becomes more likely — typically the thermostat/temperature sensor or an air flap — and it would be worth arranging an engineer rather than changing parts blindly.
